commits.subject: reel-native (SMB-REEL-NATIVE-FAULTS-2, PLR-059/060/061): an unsent FRAME tag and a bad HELLO are counted worker protocol faults; wire protocol doc matches the enforced rules

capabilities_done: PLR-059 host.rs Pool::exchange: a reply FRAME whose tag no PACKET of the session carried is Failure::Protocol (protocol_faults +1 once, worker terminated, Av1Error::Worker(Protocol); through the Registry route ReelError::DecoderFault{Protocol}). WorkerSession.sent_tags (a HashSet filled by send() for every non-empty packet before the request, one entry per packet reel feeds the session) is lent to the exchange through Call.sent and checked in the same condition as the frame-count bound and the declared-size rule, so one violation is one fail() call. Before, reel's Forward dropped such a picture without a word and the call ended Ok with a Partial receipt (Preview) or an Incomplete error (Export), nothing counted. Pre-roll pictures carry sent tags and stay legal (test worker_decode_is_bit_exact_with_in_process_and_the_dav1d_oracle, random access with pre-roll).

PLR-060 host.rs Pool::spawn: a HELLO above HELLO_CAP or made of bytes that are no frame (WireError::TooLarge or Malformed from the read) is Failure::Protocol (counted once, worker terminated, worker_protocol), like an undecodable HELLO, which now takes the same fail() path instead of a second hand-written copy of the counting. Kept as spawn_failed (worker_spawn_failed, ReelError::CodecUnavailable): end of stream before HELLO (the worker exits), silence past spawn_timeout, process creation failure and a missing pipe or I/O thread. A well-formed HELLO of another protocol version or decoder stays worker_version_mismatch.

PLR-061 wire.rs: the protocol comment replaced by the replies the host accepts per request (OPEN: OPENED or ERROR, no FRAME or BATCH_END; PACKET and FINISH: FRAMEs within the declared size and carrying a sent tag, then BATCH_END with the matching count, or ERROR; every reply echoes the request id) and the HELLO rules, each citing its test; host.rs module docs (new protocol and handshake bullets), Av1WorkerFault::Protocol and SpawnFailed docs and the lib.rs DESCRIPTOR bounds name the same rules (V4-07, the DESCRIPTOR still parses as JSON).

test-faults only (V4-04): WorkerTestFault::WrongTag (every decoded FRAME answered with the top tag bit flipped; picture, size and framing unchanged), OversizeHello (HELLO padded to twice HELLO_CAP), GarbageHello (text bytes, not a frame), MalformedHello (right kind and version, a string longer than the frame), ExitBeforeHello (exit 86 before the greeting); wire.rs encode_oversize_hello, encode_malformed_hello and GARBAGE_HELLO behind cfg(all(av1-worker, test-faults)); worker.rs Faults::on_hello, exit_before_hello and the WrongTag arm of reshape. A product worker has none of them (tests/worker_fault_env.rs unchanged and green).

adjacent_not_fixed.text: reel's decoder feeds the av1C configuration OBUs with tag u64::MAX; a picture produced from them (a frame OBU inside the av1C record, which AV1-ISOBMFF does not allow) would reach the host with a tag no packet carried and is now a counted worker protocol fault, where reel used to skip it silently. Same treatment as the declared-size rule, which already applies to such pictures since 471b679. Not measured with a crafted container (no fixture), so UNVERIFIED in practice; flagged for the lead, no code change.

the host checks that a tag was sent, not that it is the oldest unanswered one or that it was answered before: a worker that answers with the tag of an earlier packet (or twice) is not a protocol fault here; reel's Forward decides what to do with it (drain, drop). See mutant M4.
